references.text: The introduction to the section about priests with physical defects who cannot approach to offer sacrifices, which verse 21 summarizes and concludes.
The list of specific physical defects that disqualify a priest from offering sacrifices, for which verse 21 gives the general conclusion.
Another regulation concerning who may not approach the holy offerings, focusing on ritual impurity rather than physical defects.
Describes the fire offerings (אִשֵּׁי יְהוָה) that a priest with a defect is not allowed to offer according to Leviticus 21:21.
Refers to the offering as 'God's food' (לֶחֶם אֱלֹהִים), the same expression used in 21:21 regarding what a priest cannot offer.
A parallel regulation stating that animals with defects also may not be offered as God's food (לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֵיכֶם).
Aaron's sons are appointed to the priesthood, the same lineage mentioned in Leviticus 21:21.
Confirms that only Aaron's descendants may approach to offer incense before the Lord.
